domain_analysis.scope: Interior new construction stair riser and tread stain and clear coat workflows
domain_analysis.workflow_overview: Three-layer coating system for stair components: stain (color) → sanding sealer → clear topcoat (protection + depth). Stair-specific concerns include tread nosing detail work, anti-slip additive for tread safety, risers-before-treads sequence, and high-wear tread durability requirements.
key_differences_from_trim_stain: EA-based UOM (per riser, per tread) instead of LF aggregate
Two distinct items with different characteristics (risers = small/vertical, treads = larger/horizontal/high-wear)
Anti-slip additive option for tread clear coat
Tread nosing (bullnose edge) requires detail work during sanding and staining
Internal sequence: risers before treads in each phase (top-down flow)
High-wear surface (treads) benefits from extra clear coats
QT4 default (vs QT3 for trim) due to high-visibility location
No profile_complexity modifier — risers are flat, treads have nosing only
key_differences_from_paint_counterpart: This spec covers BOTH risers and treads for stain (paint counterpart covers risers + stringers, treads excluded)
No stringer — stringers routed to SF_TRIM_NC_STAIN for stain work
Bare wood input (SS_BARE) instead of primed surface
Three product roles (stain, sealer, clear) instead of one (finish)
Anti-slip additive for tread safety — paint counterpart has no equivalent
No substrate dimension (only wood for staining, vs MDF/poplar/hardwood/plywood for paint)

zones.condition: During riser work and between tread clear coats
zones.notes: Tape tread nosing during riser work. Light paper cover between tread clear coats. NOT heavy-duty Ram Board (that is paint counterpart).

state_analysis.notes: Same state model as canonical trim stain.

key_rates.riser_stain_brush_wipe: 6-7.5 EA/hr — ~8-10 min per riser including wipe. Small surface area.
key_rates.tread_stain_brush_wipe: 4-5 EA/hr — ~12-15 min per tread including wipe. Larger surface + nosing detail.
key_rates.riser_clear_brush: 7.5-10 EA/hr — ~6-8 min per riser. No wipe step.
key_rates.tread_clear_brush: 5-6 EA/hr — ~10-12 min per tread. Larger surface + nosing.
key_rates.bare_wood_sand_tread: 5-6 EA/hr — ~10-12 min per tread (includes nosing edge).

production_rate_analysis.comparison_to_paint: Stain rates include wipe step. Riser stain (~8-10 min) vs riser paint finish (~5-6 min) — stain takes longer due to wipe. Tread stain is unique to this spec (paint counterpart excludes treads).

risk_notes.risk: Stained/clear-coated treads wear faster than factory-finished flooring
risk_notes.mitigation: Minimum 2 clear coats (QT4). Anti-slip additive in final coat. Oil poly or catalyzed lacquer for maximum durability. Avoid foot traffic for 72+ hours.

risk_notes.risk: Tread nosing (bullnose) is a complex curve that sheds stain and clear
risk_notes.mitigation: Extra attention during application. Multiple thin passes on nosing. Back-brush nosing after spray.

risk_notes.topic: Stain color mismatch risers vs treads
risk_notes.risk: Different wood species between risers and treads creates color variation
risk_notes.mitigation: Same stain lot. Test on scrap from each component. Risers often a different (lighter) wood than treads — color difference may be intentional.

risk_notes.risk: Adding anti-slip to non-final clear coats creates rough surface that impairs adhesion of next coat
risk_notes.mitigation: Anti-slip in FINAL coat only. Label clearly during multi-coat application.

assumptions.value: This stain spec covers BOTH risers and treads (unlike paint counterpart which covers risers + stringers). Treads are commonly stained while risers may be painted white — this spec is for the all-stain scenario.
assumptions.note: Paint counterpart excludes treads (routed to future SF_STAIR_TREAD_NC). Stain spec includes treads because stain risers + stain treads are typically same session.

assumptions.value: Anti-slip additive mixed into final clear coat only, not intermediate coats
assumptions.note: No existing doctrine. Based on manufacturer guidelines for anti-slip additives.
